Many people may know "Ace of Spades" and nothing else, but the classic lineup hand an incalculable influence on Rock and Heavy Metal that will be felt far into the future. Countless musicians playing as hard and loud as they can cite Lemmy and the crew for helping to form their musical taste and style. Regardless of your thoughts on Metallica one of the only reasons they exist at all is because of Motörhead. And you don't need me to tell you how influential and successful they have been. Entire swaths of heavy metal bands also owe their existence to Motörhead. Early extreme metal bands took heaps of influence from Overkill and Ace of Spades, and I think it's likely that today what is normally considered underground heavy metal could have a very different look without Motörhead ever existing.

Never content to follow, Lemmy and co. always wanted to play rock and roll as fast and as loud as possible. Regardless of public taste, musical landscape, economic viability, and efforts by fans to try and place Motörhead into categories that Lemmy himself never agreed with, that's exactly what they did for four decades until Lemmy tragically succumbed to cancer. Throughout all that time they hit the road and cranked out albums and created one of the most consistent legacies of hard and fast rock you will ever hear.

Lemmy, Eddie, and Philthy started all of that and made rock music that people will listen to probably until the end of human existence. These three men were rock and roll, and lived and breathed it every single day they were together. I doubt something like Motörhead will ever truly be replicated, and now that all of them have left this world it seems a bit emptier and less fun.

But the music will live forever. Music like this always lives forever. I've been gone from this site for quite a few months now, real life has thrown a ton of shit my way. But through all of that, whenever I'm not sure what to listen to, Motörhead is almost always my first choice. I'll probably get around to posting a classic lineup playlist in a few days.

Hope Phil Campbell and Mikkey Dee stick around for quite a bit longer, but today truly marks the end of an era.
